purpose.primary: Teach learners to inspect relationships between objects, observations, representations, measurements, models, requirements, or states without forcing them to match.
purpose.learning_goal: Identify meaningful correspondences, explain what supports them, preserve mismatches and unmapped elements, and qualify relationships according to their evidence, boundary, and conditions.
purpose.principle: Alignment is not making things match. It is making their relationship visible enough to know where they correspond, where they do not, and why.

position_in_aaccc.dependency: Alignment should operate on objects, observations, assumptions, boundaries, and unknowns made sufficiently visible through Awareness.

primary_questions: Why am I comparing these things?
Under what conditions does the relationship hold?

correspondence_not_identity.principle: A representation may correspond usefully to something without being identical to it.

key_distinctions.principle: A maps to B does not automatically mean A is B.
Superficial resemblance is not sufficient evidence of meaningful correspondence.
Matching words can hide different definitions.
Different vocabulary may still refer to closely corresponding concepts.
Observers do not need identical reports for their observations to align with different observer positions.
A difference should be preserved before deciding whether it is a mistake.
Structural resemblance does not establish provenance or causal influence.
A useful mapping may preserve only part of the represented structure.
Matching field names do not establish that the fields mean the same thing.
A passing example may align with only part of a broader requirement.

comparison_boundary.principle: Alignment judgments depend on what aspects are actually being compared.

purpose.question: What is this comparison for?
purpose.principle: A representation may align strongly for one purpose and poorly for another.

layered_alignment.principle: A relationship may be strong at one layer and weak at another.
layered_alignment.lesson: One successful correspondence should not leak into unrelated layers.

same_word_different_meaning.lesson: The labels align while the meanings do not.

different_words_similar_meaning.principle: Vocabulary difference alone does not settle conceptual alignment.

evidence.principle: An important mapping should expose what supports it.

example.evidence: coordinates correspond to the entrance location

assumptions.principle: Some alignments depend on conventions or labels rather than independently verified relationships.

example.label: final_report.pdf
example.assumption: the filename accurately describes the current contents

assumptions.question: What must be true for this mapping to work?

partial_alignment.definition: Meaningful correspondence exists while important differences remain.

conditional_alignment.definition: The correspondence holds under a stated condition.
conditional_alignment.example: This documentation aligns with software version 2.1.

uncertain_alignment.definition: A correspondence is plausible but not adequately established by available evidence.
uncertain_alignment.principle: Do not upgrade uncertainty merely because a neat mapping would be useful.

misalignment.definition: Important relationships conflict under the selected comparison boundary.
misalignment.principle: The mismatch itself may identify what deserves another look.

unmapped.definition: No useful correspondence has been established for an element.
unmapped.principle: Leave unmapped elements unmapped rather than inventing a partner to complete the table.

alignment_states.meaning: Important relationships within the chosen boundary correspond well and have useful support.
Useful correspondences exist while important differences remain.
The mapping holds under stated conditions.
The relationship is plausible but insufficiently established.
Important relationships conflict under the chosen boundary.
No useful correspondence has yet been established.

mismatch.principle: Preserve differences before explaining or repairing them.

tolerance.principle: Numerical closeness does not define Alignment by itself.

should_these_match.principle: Before repairing a mismatch, determine whether strong correspondence is actually expected.
examples: two descriptions from opposite sides of an object

observer_alignment.principle: Observer positions should be mapped before observer reports are treated as contradictory.
observer_alignment.lesson: Different layers may produce observations that are simultaneously accurate.

scale.principle: A representation may align at one scale and fail at another.

pattern: documentation <-> current software becomes partial or misaligned

asymmetry.principle: A useful representation from A to B does not guarantee an equally useful representation from B to A.
asymmetry.example: A summary may represent a report for a purpose, while the report is not simply a representation of the summary.

information_loss.principle: Mapping one representation into another may preserve selected structure while losing other information.
information_loss.question: Was the loss acceptable for the intended purpose?

example.may_correspond_to: air temperature near the sensor at measurement time

measurement_alignment.principle: A measurement has a spatial, temporal, and methodological boundary.

data_alignment.principle: Matching schemas can hide different meanings.

example.requirement: Users must be able to export their data.
example.implementation: Download the current screen as an image.

test_alignment.lesson: A passing test can provide valid evidence while covering only part of a broader requirement.

questions: Which aspect of the concept does this measurement represent?
Does the source actually support the attributed claim?
Is the attributed claim adjacent but different?
source_alignment.principle: Good provenance depends on good Alignment.

similarity_vs_provenance.principle: Two ideas may resemble one another without one causing or influencing the other.
similarity_vs_provenance.safe_statement_without_lineage: These structures share a resemblance in how they organize the problem.

analogy.principle: An analogy preserves selected relationships and has a boundary.
analogy.warning: A useful analogy should not quietly become a theory.

explore.purpose: Move from noticing resemblance to identifying specific, bounded, evidence-supported correspondence.
explore.primary_habit: Replace these seem similar with these correspond in this specific way.

explore_questions: What does the representation leave out?

practice.purpose: Practice constructing evidence-supported mappings while preserving mismatch, uncertainty, direction, conditionality, and information loss.

patterns: A corresponds to B for the purpose of...

student_record.name: Alignment Record
student_record.purpose: Make the relationship between two objects, descriptions, models, or states inspectable.
student_record.principle: Use enough structure to explain why the mapping received its current qualification.

guide.symptom: The chain skips when the rider pedals hard.

observed_bicycle: The chain skips under heavy pedaling.
The rear derailleur appears visually aligned.
Several rear sprocket teeth show wear.
The bicycle shifts normally during light pedaling.
Chain wear has not been measured.
Derailleur adjustment has not been tested.
Not every drivetrain component has been inspected.

mastery.goal: Inspect how far the guide and observed bicycle align without diagnosing the bicycle or forcing the guide to fit.

mastery_boundary.comparing: guide symptom, proposed cause, and recommended action against observed drivetrain behavior and visible condition
mastery_boundary.not_comparing: every possible cause of chain skipping or the complete condition of the bicycle

mastery_cause_mapping.reason: Visual appearance neither directly confirms nor fully rules out the proposed adjustment issue.

mastery_mismatch.observed_extra_structure: visible wear elsewhere in the drivetrain
mastery_mismatch.interpretation: The observed system contains information not represented by the guide excerpt.

mastery_action_boundary.action_justification: not yet strongly established from the supplied observations
mastery_action_boundary.principle: Do not let symptom Alignment silently become cause or action Alignment.

mastery_possible_assumptions: The skipping is caused by derailleur adjustment.
Visual appearance does not rule out an adjustment problem.
Visible drivetrain wear is not the primary cause.
The guide symptom description applies to this drivetrain.

reason: The proposed cause is not equivalently supported.
Visible wear remains unmapped to the guide explanation.
Additional observation is needed before the recommended action can be strongly aligned with the observed problem.

mastery_criteria: separate symptom Alignment from cause Alignment

if_learner_says_nothing_aligns.example: Symptom Alignment may be strong even when cause Alignment is unresolved.

may_ask: identify a condition required for Alignment

badge.name: Alignment Badge
badge.meaning: I can examine how things correspond without forcing them to match.

recommended_prompts: Find a mismatch I may have overlooked.
Give me the strongest reasonable counter-mapping.
Which mapping depends on the strongest assumption?
Label these mappings as strong, partial, conditional, uncertain, or unsupported.

ai_over_alignment_risk.warning: Pattern abundance is not evidence quality.
ai_over_alignment_risk.question: What relationship makes this mapping meaningful beyond superficial similarity?

formal_companion.formal_question: What relationship actually permits this correspondence or substitution?
formal_companion.boundary: Formal equality is one strict kind of Alignment and does not represent every partial, conditional, directional, or uncertain human-facing mapping.

awareness_inside_alignment.question: What did each object or observer actually provide before mapping?

bridge_to_coherence.next_question: Can all of these mappings hold together?
bridge_to_coherence.principle: Individually plausible correspondences may create a globally incoherent structure.

alignment_is_not: find as many similarities as possible
equate matching labels with matching meanings

provenance.transformation: Four human-facing Alignment documents compacted into one structured AI learning object.
do_not_infer: complete coverage from one passing test
global representation from one local measurement

must: Identify exactly what is being compared.
Declare or inspect the comparison boundary.
Name the specific relationship supporting a correspondence.
Qualify partial, conditional, or uncertain relationships.
Recognize mapping direction and information loss when relevant.
Return to Awareness when the objects or observation boundaries are unclear.
must_not: infer historical influence from structural similarity
treat the same label as proof of the same meaning
treat different labels as proof of different meaning
upgrade a symptom match into cause alignment
upgrade a passing example into full requirement coverage
require Lean or AI for mastery
